producer_report.summary: Reordered docs/design/roadmap.md. A new first step, RM-0 "Accelerate Athena", cites the BRIEF.md 2026-10-13 "Athena owns acceleration" addendum (lines 494-496). It covers the sccache hit rate, parallel jobs including CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md collisions, native PR landing, and timings fed back. Each has its own "done when" test. The 0-hit sccache figure is labelled as user-reported, not measured. RM-6 (firstmate study) is stated to run alongside RM-0. The "How the order was chosen" paragraph is rewritten. The old RM-8 rows (A4-3, A5-3, A5-4, A5-5, SD-6, AD-4, AD-5, AD-9) and AD-11 moved into RM-0 and were removed from RM-8 and RM-2, so each row appears once. RM-8 no longer exists and the other numbers are unchanged. The roadmap now says 13 steps and 104 rows. I updated the strategy-view "What to do next" text and the requirements-map roadmap bullet. I added a CHANGELOG entry and decision D83. Docs only.

checks_run.note: All test binaries reported ok, no failures.
Only the five documentation files are modified.

open_issues: README.md was not edited because nothing in it was inconsistent.
The first cargo test run's output was truncated, so I reran it with -q to see the results.
The requirements-map row for AD-11 is unchanged; its status stays Partial.
mistakes: I did not diagnose the sccache 0-hit cause. The candidate causes in RM-0 (wrapper not applied, per-job target dir or path differences, CARGO_INCREMENTAL) are my guesses and are labelled as examples to check, not findings.
learnings: Of the three docs the brief names, only strategy-view.md mentions step order ('first three steps'). requirements-map.md and README.md had no RM-n or step-number references; README's roadmap pointer is generic and needed no change.
docs/decisions.md has no index; entries are appended as '## Dnn' sections, and D82 was the last.
The step count of 13 holds after the reorder: RM-0 to RM-7 and RM-9 to RM-13.
desires: A tool to read tool-result files that the harness persists outside the working directory.
